ios: The iOS application also covers iPadOS; both have identical audited API availability and app control paths.

Four configuration fields remain constrained UI presets backed by bundled JS/CSS resources: uiManagerFactoryFunction, playerUiJs, playerUiCss and userInterfaceConfig. Missing custom resources fall back to the SDK UI; source URLs and HLS/MP4 type are editable.
Eight runtime control candidates are sdk-ui-unverified; their evidence identifies only the native SDK UI container.
SourceConfig.cmcdConfig requires OS 18 or later and TweaksConfig.includeMachineGeneratedSubtitles requires OS 27 or later; family-wide availability retains both.
tvos: The UI variant picker is excluded on tvOS and System UI is fixed. The native full-screen editor exposes the same 11 configuration leaves as iOS; there are no configuration presets.

The app-owned tvOS remote Play/Pause command maps to Player.play() and Player.pause(). Opaque System UI controls do not receive volume, track or fullscreen credit without exact binding and runtime evidence.
SDK APIs documented as no-op on tvOS remain in the available denominator when their Swift declaration permits tvOS.

scopeNotes: Bounded public BitmovinPlayerCore operational scope: 65 configuration or nested input owners, 39 runtime owners, and four typed listener families. This is not a percentage of every SDK declaration.
The denominator is extracted from pinned vendor DocC independently of the app mapping; available deprecated APIs remain counted.

Configuration counts public fields of the selected roots and nested input types. Initializers, enum cases, pure output data, inherited SwiftUI View APIs, and Analytics/Collector modules are outside this scope.
Availability is the declared platform-family surface, not a guarantee that every member exists at the app minimum OS version. Per-symbol introduction metadata is retained in sdk-symbols.json.

Direct means an app-owned control accepts arbitrary supported arguments or invokes an argumentless operation. Preset means a fixed set of sources, values or UI choices; it does not imply arbitrary argument support.

Namespace containers remain code-only; only individually mapped leaves receive GUI credit. Allow DVR controls changes an app DvrKit flag, while the separate SDK time shift control changes PlaybackConfig.isTimeShiftEnabled.

Observed getters and event subscriptions receive no configurable or command coverage credit. Player.timeShift is also displayed indirectly, but its single command row is not duplicated as an observation.

Concrete Event types emitted by the four typed listener families are individual event identities. Generic callbacks and abstract event bases are excluded; public listener registration APIs remain separate runtime rows.
Five event identities are monitored: SourceLoaded, TimeShifted, DvrWindowExceeded and PlaybackFinished have named log entries; TimeChanged triggers DVR refresh. Event payload fields are not exposed.
App-owned configuration controls and derived displays have exact source bindings. SDK-supplied UI controls receive no direct or preset credit without exact binding and runtime evidence.

On 2026-10-21, native GUI checks on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV simulators applied source/startup settings and played the local 60-second HLS and progressive MP4 fixtures with advancing native positions and visible video. Native getters checked the applied start offset, autoplay, bitrate cap and forward-buffer values. Controlled HLS completion checks on iPhone and Apple TV retained the same source and disabled app DVR after PlaybackFinished, even when SDK live/infinite getters persisted; replay and new-source resets were checked separately. These checks do not establish physical-device behavior, audible synchronization, network bitrate enforcement, casting, offline playback or Analytics receipt.

11 configuration leaves have app-owned editors: source URL, HLS/MP4 type, title, poster URL, start offset in seconds and timeline reference, autoplay, startup mute, SDK time shift, maximum bitrate in bit/s and forward buffer in seconds. Validated Apply reloads source-only changes or recreates the player for startup settings, retaining source options, UI mode, logs and the app DVR switch; playback position resets. Reset to applied changes only the draft.
